The Ramsey number $R(K_5, K_{5-e})$ is the smallest integer $n$ such that every $2$-coloring of the edges of the complete graph $K_n$ (say, red and blue) contains either a red complete graph $K_5$ or a blue graph isomorphic to $K_{5-e}$ (the complete graph on $5$ vertices with one edge removed).

According to the survey of small Ramsey numbers (e.g., Stanisław Radziszowski, *Small Ramsey Numbers*, Electronic Journal of Combinatorics), the exact value of $R(K_5, K_{5-e})$ has not been determined and remains an open problem in Ramsey theory. Only nontrivial lower and upper bounds are currently known.
